long.title: The Oldest Song Ever Found (3,400 Years Old) — And What It Sounds Like
long.description:
In 1928, a farmer's plow hit a stone on the coast of Syria. Underneath was a lost city, and decades later, the oldest song ever written down.

This is the story of Hurrian Hymn No. 6: a 3,400-year-old clay tablet with lyrics, lyre instructions and the scribe's own signature. How it survived a city burning, why nobody agrees on how to read it, and our own lyre tribute to how it might have sounded.

💬 What's the oldest song YOU know by heart? Tell us in the comments.
🔔 Subscribe for more stories behind the sounds: https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCBwPlLWZ-b_ZAUWiPOhEg1w?sub_confirmation=1
▶️ Next on MJ Sound Chronicles: The Cursed Trumpets of Tutankhamun.
